messages:
jess: Hey @mike_payroll — I noticed my Feb 15 paycheck net was ~30% lower than expected. I moved from CA to NY on Feb 10 and updated ADP, but paystub shows CA state tax for full period. Can you confirm?

mike_payroll: Thanks for flagging, Jess. Do you have the employee ID and the payrun ID? I can pull the record quickly.

jess: EmpID 45872, payrun 2026-02-15-PR.

mike_payroll: pulling it now...

payroll-bot: Log snippet for payrun 2026-02-15-PR: 
```
2026-02-15 03:22:10 PAYROLL processed EMP=45872 STATE=CA TAX_CODE=STD_WITHHOLD AMOUNT=$142.87
2026-02-15 03:22:10 PAYROLL fallback STATE_RESIDENCY=NY effective_date=2026-02-10
2026-02-15 03:22:10 ADJ_PENDING state_mismatch_flag=true
```

mike_payroll: Looks like the system applied CA withholding despite the residency change. The residency effective date is captured but the tax jurisdiction on the run stayed CA. That's why net pay is off.

tara_finance: Tagging in — if we correct this retroactively we need to reverse the CA withhold and reapply NY withhold for the days in Feb. That will affect both YTD state withholding and employer filings. We usually do a corrective payrun in the next payroll cycle.

alex_hr: @jess sorry for the hassle. Did you submit the state change through the relocation form + ADP? We had a couple of transfers where the relocation form didn't reach payroll queue.

jess: I filled the relocation form on Feb 9 and updated address in ADP on Feb 10. I also Slack-DM'd People Ops but maybe it didn't arrive.

mike_payroll: OK — process wise: 1) We'll create an off-cycle adjustment for 02/15 reversing CA withholding and applying NY. 2) We'll update the payrun metadata so W-2 prep is correct (NY vs CA split). 3) We'll notify you before the reversal posts. ETA for the correction: next business payroll cycle (within 5 days).

sam_engineer: Quick Q — will this show up as an extra line on my next stub or as a separate ACH? Want to know for budgeting.

mike_payroll: It will show as an adjustment line on your next paycheck, not a separate ACH. Net will be credited back (if we over-withheld) and NY withholding applied. If the adjustment causes an extra net liability to employee, we'll email options (net pay correction vs. withholding offset).

tara_finance: Also FYI — if the CA withholding was reported already to state (unlikely for mid-month), we may need to file an amended return or W-2c at year end. We'll mark this for the W-2 reconciliation queue.

alex_hr: For audit trail, @jess can you forward the relocation confirmation email you got (timestamped) to payroll@redwood.com? That helps expedite.

jess: Sent it just now.

mike_payroll: Got it. Thanks — I'll queue the off-cycle correction and follow up here once scheduled. 

jess: Appreciate it :relieved: Please confirm when posted so I can verify the next stub.

mike_payroll: Will do. Leaving a ticket: PR-7421 (internal). Adding notes: "mid-pay-period state change, off-cycle correction pending, employee provided relocation form 2026-02-09."

payroll-bot: Ticket PR-7421 created by mike_payroll at 2026-02-15 09:10:12. Status: open.

tara_finance: Marking for W-2 reconciliation.

mike_payroll: Closing loop: correction scheduled for 2026-02-20 run. Expect updated stub same day. I'll post confirmation when complete.

jess: Thanks all!

mike_payroll: Confirmed — correction completed 2026-02-20 14:06. Net refund $130.12 posted; NY withholding $12.45 applied. Updated YTD state withholding reflects NY. We'll include PR-7421 notes in year-end W-2 review.

jess: I can see it, thanks. All good on my end. :thumbsup:
